analysis: The broad option retains a substantial psychological and cognitive core, with social theory, organisational psychology, philosophy and research as complementary perspectives. Removed molecular gateway and physiology from this broad option in favour of organisational psychology and modern sociology. All course claims were reconsidered against their actual profile or description.

The clinical-health option retains psychological and social foundations alongside epidemiology, physiology and pharmacology, with the latter serving bounded neural-treatment and health roles. Replaced generic disease pathology with philosophical emotion inquiry. The cognitive/data option removes cell biology, generic laboratory, molecular pathology and systemic disease emphasis in favour of empirical methods, clinical assessment, AI ethics, philosophy and social behaviour.

All three Psycholinguistics conflicts are resolved through its sole 2027h1 offering after the brain gateway. Research methods precedes statistics; psychopathology precedes assessment; data foundations precede advanced computational work. Each pair passes the thirty-credit floor and differs substantively in academic weight.

Thirteen bounded primary alignments replace broad and false correspondences. Qualitative research is not correlational statistics, philosophical selfhood is not personality psychology, data cleaning is not experimental design, and evidence synthesis is not the empirical research practicum. Clinical assessment is the primary placement for the combined UCR diagnostic/therapy course; it is not counted again for treatment or test theory. Optional research remains outside scheduled credits.

ACCPPDE101.name: Personal & Professional Development
ACCPPDE101.contribution: Academic writing, literature evaluation, civic collaboration and reflective practice provide the first-year common foundation.

BENGATE102.name: Research Methods & Statistics
BENGATE102.contribution: develops empirical research design, measurement, sampling, statistics and a complete ethically managed student data-collection project

BENLEAD311.name: Psychology of Organizations & Leadership
BENLEAD311.contribution: examines personality, motivation, perception, emotions, groups and organisational behaviour, including research planning and systematic literature review

DISARIN111.name: AI Ethics
DISARIN111.contribution: examines AI ethics through psychological perspectives on development, clinical care, social interaction and cognition, including an analytical psychology project and research-grounded podcast

DISDATA111.name: Introduction to Data Science
DISDATA111.contribution: develops data import, cleaning, transformation, visualisation and applied research in R, supporting analysis of behavioural evidence

DISDATA211.name: Machine Learning
DISDATA211.contribution: develops regression, classification, resampling and model evaluation for prediction and empirical data analysis; this is statistical learning rather than specialist psychological test theory

DISDATA212.name: Image Processing & Computer Vision
DISDATA212.contribution: develops computational image filtering, segmentation, recognition and evaluation in Python and OpenCV, providing computational methods complementary to biological perception

GOSPHIL212.name: Ethics
GOSPHIL212.contribution: examines moral theories and ethical reasoning, enabling evaluation of values and competing interests in childrearing and education

GOSPHIL214.name: Philosophy of Mind
GOSPHIL214.contribution: examines mind, self, identity and consciousness through philosophical arguments and neuropsychological cases, complementing psychological accounts of development

GOSPHIL311.name: Philosophy of Emotion
GOSPHIL311.contribution: examines emotion through philosophical theories, cognition, ethics, social life and political action; it complements clinical emotion research without claiming therapeutic training

GOSPHIL313.name: Free Will, Time & the Self
GOSPHIL313.contribution: examines agency, determinism, time and selfhood, including scientific challenges and addiction; philosophical agency is not personality-trait psychology

GOSSOCI111.name: Introduction to Sociology
GOSSOCI111.contribution: examines social identities, institutions, boundaries and inequality as the wider context of family, school and peer life

GOSSOCI212.name: Qualitative Research Methodology
GOSSOCI212.contribution: develops qualitative interviewing, documentary inquiry, interpretation and reflexivity for studying social experiences and institutions

GOSSOCI214.name: Modern Sociology
GOSSOCI214.contribution: examines modern social theory, power, inequality and cultural context through competing traditions and an empirical case paper

GOSSOCI311.name: New Issues in Contemporary Social Theory
GOSSOCI311.contribution: examines trust, solidarity, civil society, public spheres and social repair through theory and research on an organisation or initiative

HCBBIOM111.name: Epidemiology & Public Health
HCBBIOM111.contribution: examines population health, inequality, epidemiological designs, confounding and intervention evaluation as methods for studying developmental risk and prevention

HCBBIOM311.name: Pharmacology
HCBBIOM311.contribution: examines drug action, including neural and psychoactive treatment mechanisms and an experimental proposal; it supplies bounded biological treatment foundations rather than professional child therapy

HCBCOGN112.name: Neurobiology
HCBCOGN112.contribution: develops neural and cellular explanations of nervous-system function as biological foundations for cognition and developmental differences

HCBCOGN212.name: Perception & Action
HCBCOGN212.contribution: examines neural mechanisms of perception and action, complementing the cognitive and biological study of development

HCBCOGN311.name: Higher Order Functions
HCBCOGN311.contribution: examines attention, memory, emotion, control and social cognition, including an attentional-blink experiment and research proposal

HCBCOGN312.name: Psycholinguistics
HCBCOGN312.contribution: examines language acquisition and processing, reading, dyslexia and language impairments using psycholinguistic evidence and experimental methods

HCBGATE101.name: Foundation of Life, Health & Biomedicine
HCBGATE101.contribution: introduces cellular, molecular and genetic foundations needed for the selected physiology and pharmacology sequence; it supports the biological strand rather than serving as child pedagogy

HCBGATE102.name: Introduction to Brain & Behavior
HCBGATE102.contribution: introduces brain and behaviour relationships as a foundation for developmental, cognitive and psychological inquiry

HCBLIFE212.name: Human Physiology
HCBLIFE212.contribution: examines organ systems, homeostasis and stress responses as biological context for health, behaviour and supportive interventions

HCBPSYC111.name: Social Psychology
HCBPSYC111.contribution: studies social influence, identity, group processes, prejudice, prosocial behaviour and close relationships through empirical psychological research

HCBPSYC211.name: Statistics & Experimental Methods
HCBPSYC211.contribution: develops experimental design, statistical modelling, assumption checks and interpretation in health and behavioural research

HCBPSYC212.name: Psychopathology
HCBPSYC212.contribution: examines psychopathology across the lifespan, classification, biopsychosocial explanations and treatment, using cases and critical literature synthesis

HCBPSYC311.name: Medical & Health Psychology
HCBPSYC311.contribution: examines health, illness, prevention, stress and healthcare relationships, with culturally attentive interviewing and clinical-health case formulation

HCBPSYC312.name: Psychodiagnostics & Psychotherapies
HCBPSYC312.contribution: introduces diagnostic reasoning, tests and interviews, ethics and major psychotherapies, with introductory assessment practice and an integrated case report

HCBPSYC313.name: Advanced Research Methods & Statistics
HCBPSYC313.contribution: develops systematic review and meta-analysis, bias appraisal, effect-size calculation and evidence synthesis for behavioural and health questions

HCBPSYC314.name: Lifespan Developmental Psychology
HCBPSYC314.contribution: examines physical, cognitive, emotional, social and personality development from prenatal life onward, including attachment, education, culture and developmental psychopathology

HCBPSYC315.name: Youth Resilience to Extremism
HCBPSYC315.contribution: studies adolescent risk, belonging and prevention of extremism and produces research-based teacher-training materials and a youth toolkit for an inclusive school project

MCCCOMM311.name: Persuasive Communication
MCCCOMM311.contribution: examines persuasion, framing and ethical communication through community projects, supporting responsible public explanation and youth-support communication

alignment.rationale: Both develop empirical research design, measurement, sampling and evaluation of evidence. UCR also includes statistics and a research project.

Both critically examine mind, consciousness, self and accounts of mental states.
Both examine theories of emotion and its relationships with cognition, action and social life. Tilburg also includes clinical emotion regulation and treatment applications.
Both introduce sociological theories, institutions, social relationships and inequality.
Both examine biological and neural mechanisms underlying psychological processes.
Both study perception and action as psychological processes using their scientific foundations. UCR emphasises neural mechanisms and neuropsychological interpretation.
Both connect brain structure and neural processes with psychological functions and behaviour.
Both study social cognition, influence, groups and interpersonal behaviour through psychological research.
Both develop regression modelling, statistical assumptions and interpretation of behavioural evidence. UCR also develops experimental-design and other statistical methods.
Both examine classification, explanations and treatment of mental disorders.

Both develop diagnostic reasoning, interviews, test administration and interpretation, ethics and case integration. UCR combines introductory assessment with psychotherapy rather than offering the complete specialist assessment course.
Both examine physical, cognitive, emotional and social development across life stages and its theoretical explanations.
